facts.text: Experts disagree on the primary collision-mitigation trigger: road practice favors time to collision and time to brake, ISO 21815-3 frames risk areas sized by stopping ability, and research also uses probabilistic risk scores. There is no universal agreement on one metric.
facts.quote: Road practice favors time to collision and time to brake; ISO 21815-3 frames risk areas sized by stopping ability; probabilistic risk scores are also used in research. There is no universal agreement on one metric.

facts.text: Within the disagreement over collision-mitigation trigger metrics, expert opinion identifies a hybrid stopping-margin and risk-zone method, with time to collision as a supplemental feature, as the strongest technical case for heavy off-road machines, rather than relying primarily on road practice's time-to-collision and time-to-brake metrics.
facts.quote: The strongest technical case for this application is a hybrid stopping-margin and risk-zone method with time to collision as a supplemental feature.

facts.text: The disagreement over whether the highest-fidelity model is the best production threshold model is challenged by the 2026 round robin: detailed models can produce more variation than prescribed point-mass models. This result is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: The 2026 round robin shows detailed models can produce more variation than prescribed point-mass models

facts.text: Rather than automatically choosing the highest-fidelity production threshold model, expert opinion favors the lowest-fidelity model that predicts every safety-relevant output within a validated uncertainty envelope.
facts.quote: the correct fidelity is the lowest model that predicts every safety-relevant output within a validated uncertainty envelope.

facts.text: Epiroc's Titan page claims "full level 7, 8 and 9" capability using EMESRT PR-5A as a guideline, but recommends evaluation without immediately enforcing Level 9 intervention; South African practice, by contrast, pushes Level 9 mandates.
facts.quote: Epiroc's Titan page claims "full level 7, 8 and 9" capability with EMESRT PR-5A as a guideline yet recommends running evaluation "without immediately enforcing level-9 intervention"; South African practice, by contrast, pushes Level 9 mandates.

facts.text: Sources disagree on assumed reaction times for machine-motion and brake-timing analysis, with assumptions ranging from 0.5 s to 2.5 s.
facts.quote: *Assumed reaction times* range from 0.5 s to 2.5 s across sources

facts.text: NIOSH (2022) identifies a mismatch in intervention research: most system literature addresses vehicle-to-vehicle collisions, whereas most haul-truck fatalities involve vehicle-to-environment collisions, such as driving through a berm.
facts.quote: NIOSH (2022) notes most system literature addresses vehicle-to-vehicle collisions while most haul-truck fatalities are vehicle-to-environment, such as driving through a berm

facts.text: In contrast to intervention literature's predominant focus on vehicle-to-vehicle collisions, NIOSH's 2020 roadmap found loss of control to be the most common initiating event in fatal accidents, accounting for 33 of 91 fatal accidents.
facts.quote: NIOSH's 2020 roadmap found loss of control the most common initiating event (33 of 91 fatal accidents).
